mechanism: The handler's lambda list is (node ((inputs :array) outputs (locktime :or 0))) at src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:843: arguments 4 (replaceable) and 5 (version) are named in our own tables (src/rpc/core-tables.lisp:28,211) but never destructured, so they are discarded. The per-input sequence default is the literal #xffffffff (:864) and the transaction version is the literal 2 (:896). Core's AddInputs (refs/bitcoin/src/rpc/rawtransaction_util.cpp:47-56) chooses MAX_BIP125_RBF_SEQUENCE (0xfffffffd, util/rbf.h:12) whenever rbf.value_or(true), and createrawtransaction leaves rbf as nullopt when the argument is absent (rpc/rawtransaction.cpp:396-399), so 0xfffffffd is the DEFAULT; only replaceable=false falls through to MAX_SEQUENCE_NONFINAL (0xfffffffe) when nLockTime is set, else SEQUENCE_FINAL. ConstructTransaction (rawtransaction_util.cpp:147-171) also takes version, defaulting to DEFAULT_RAWTX_VERSION = CTransaction::CURRENT_VERSION, and rejects anything outside TX_MIN_STANDARD_VERSION..TX_MAX_STANDARD_VERSION = 1..3 (policy/policy.h:151-152), and it rejects an explicit replaceable=true whose supplied sequences contradict it.
consequence: The transaction handed back is wrong in three ways at once, and only the caller's own inspection would reveal it. (1) A transaction built with a locktime is consensus-FINAL: all-0xffffffff sequences make nLockTime unenforceable, so an operator who asked for a timelocked transaction gets one that can be mined immediately - the field is present in the serialization (f4010000 for locktime 500), which is what makes it convincing. (2) The RBF default is inverted relative to Core: a caller who names nothing gets a non-signalling transaction where Core gives a replaceable one, and a caller who passes replaceable=false gets the same bytes, so the argument is inert in both directions. (3) version=3 silently produces a v2 transaction with different relay policy, and an out-of-range version is never rejected. A wrong transaction a client acts on: S2. Not S1 - the output is unsigned and the caller can still set sequence per input through the input object, which our loop does honour.
evidence: Probe ga11v-rpcutil-p1 (scratch, not committed), through bl.rpc:dispatch-rpc-method with bl.rpc::%normalize-rpc-params, one input and one OP_RETURN output. no-arguments, replaceable=true, version=3 and version=99 all return the identical hex 020000000101...ffffffff010000000000000000066a040001020300000000 - version 02000000, sequence ffffffff, locktime 0. locktime=500 and (locktime=500, replaceable=false) return the identical hex ...ffffffff...f4010000: locktime 500 carried, sequence still ffffffff. Core for the same calls: sequence fdffffff by default (0xfffffffd), feffffff for replaceable=false with locktime 500, version 03000000 for version=3, and -8 'Invalid parameter, version out of range(1~3)' for version=99. Note the same tree already implements Core's rule correctly one file over: %PSBT-DEFAULT-SEQUENCE (src/wallet/psbt.lisp:36-42) returns 0xfffffffd / 0xfffffffe / 0xffffffff exactly as AddInputs does, and createpsbt (src/wallet/psbt.lisp:105-119) reads its replaceable argument - so createrawtransaction is the one caller of Core's ConstructTransaction contract that was left behind. Ours: src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:843,864,896; src/rpc/core-tables.lisp:28,211. Core at d3056bc: rpc/rawtransaction_util.cpp:25-71,147-171; rpc/rawtransaction.cpp:87-124,396-401; util/rbf.h:12; policy/policy.h:151-152.
fix_shape: Widen the define-rpc lambda list to (inputs outputs locktime replaceable version) and route the body through the sequence rule that already exists: call %PSBT-DEFAULT-SEQUENCE (or lift it into the shared rawtransaction helper next to PARSE-OUTPUTS, since Core keeps one AddInputs for createrawtransaction, createpsbt and walletcreatefundedpsbt) with replaceable defaulting to TRUE when the argument is absent - positional-bool-or, so explicit false is distinguishable from omitted, which is the whole point of Core's std::optional<bool>. Take the version argument with default 2, reject it outside 1..3 with Core's message 'Invalid parameter, version out of range(1~3)', and set the transaction's version from it instead of the literal. Finally port ConstructTransaction's last check: when replaceable was explicitly true and the supplied sequences do not signal, answer -8 'Invalid parameter combination: Sequence number(s) contradict replaceable option'.
